title: Remove Digit From Number to Maximize Result
statement: The string `number` holds the decimal digits of a positive integer, and `digit` is a single digit character that appears in `number` at least once. Delete exactly one copy of `digit` from `number`, choosing which copy so that the remaining string, read as a decimal integer, is as large as possible, and return that remaining string.
constraints: number contains only the digits '1' to '9'
digit is one of the digits '1' to '9'
digit appears in number at least once
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every copy of `digit` and keeping the biggest result works, since all results have the same length and can be compared as strings. A single pass is enough, though. Compare deleting the copy at `i` with deleting a later copy: both results match before `i`, and at position `i` the first shows `number[i + 1]` while the second still shows `digit`. So if the next character is larger than `digit`, deleting at `i` beats every later choice; otherwise a later copy is at least as good. If no copy is followed by a larger character, the last copy is best.

## Approach

1. Walk `number` from left to right with index `i`, skipping characters that are not `digit`.
2. Record each copy's position in `lastIndex`.
3. If the character after this copy is larger than `digit`, delete this copy and return at once.
4. If the loop finishes, delete the copy at `lastIndex`.

## Example 1, step by step

`number = "123"`, `digit = "3"`. Indexes 0 and 1 hold `1` and `2`, so they are skipped. Index 2 holds `3`: `lastIndex = 2`, but nothing follows it, so the loop ends. Deleting index 2 leaves `"12"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one scan plus one slice to build the result.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- Deleting the first copy is not always right: in `"9898"` with `9`, the best answer `"988"` deletes the last copy.
- When the next character equals `digit`, deleting either copy gives the same string, so keep scanning rather than stopping.
- Converting to a number to compare overflows at 100 digits; compare characters or equal-length strings instead.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | the index being examined |
| `lastIndex` | position of the most recent copy of `digit` seen so far |

narration.2: No copy of digit has been seen yet.
narration.3: Scan the number from the most significant digit to the least.
narration.4: Characters other than digit cannot be removed...
narration.7: Remember this copy; if nothing better turns up, the last copy is the one to delete.
narration.8: If the next character is larger than digit, deleting this copy moves it up one place and makes the number bigger than any later deletion could.
narration.9: Return the number with this copy cut out.
narration.12: No copy was followed by a larger digit, so deleting the last copy keeps the high positions as large as possible.
